items.title:
Build a polished responsive web application called “SIMCARD” for IdentityMD agents.

Core experience:

* The homepage must have one prominent search field that accepts an IdentityMD NFT token ID, such as 222.
* When the user presses Enter or clicks “Generate SIMCARD”, retrieve the NFT and agent’s public data and create a personalized animated SIMCARD.
* Every NFT must produce its own card using that NFT’s original artwork and dominant colors. Do not use a generic avatar.
* No wallet connection should be required to search or create a card.

Data sources:

* Use the public IdentityMD API at https://api.imd.fun and the Explorer API at https://explorer.imd.fun.
* Use GET /seats/:tokenId for the owner, agent ID, online status, attempts, accepted, rejected, failed, work, reviews and collaborators.
* Use GET /seats/:tokenId/standing for presence, dispatch eligibility and currently running jobs.
* Use GET /api/agents/:tokenId on the Explorer origin for owner name, held duration, jobs and last accepted activity.
* Use GET /seats/records to calculate rankings when possible.
* Use GET /wallets/:address/earnings to show public IMD earnings and launch allocations after resolving the NFT owner.
* Use public Ethereum NFT metadata or tokenURI for the original IdentityMD artwork.
* Reproduce the useful public information shown by Swarm Ledger, but do not scrape private information. If a data point cannot be verified from an official public API or onchain source, label it “Unavailable” rather than inventing it.

Animated SIMCARD:

* Display NFT number, original NFT artwork, verified agent status, online/offline/working state, agent ID, accepted work, total attempts, acceptance rate, runtime when publicly available, owner ENS or public handle, Ethereum network and last activity.
* Animate the original NFT artwork subtly: rotating orbital lines, pulsing center light, scanning line and live online indicator.
* The animation state must reflect real status: calm for ready, faster for working and dimmed for offline.
* Do not expose full wallet addresses by default. Show a shortened address only inside the expanded details view.
* Include a real QR code linking to the public SIMCARD profile URL for that NFT.

Interaction:

* Clicking the card must open a detailed agent profile containing payouts, allocations, work history, acceptance statistics, rank, reviews and onchain verification links whenever those fields are publicly available.
* Include links to IdentityMD Explorer, Etherscan and OpenSea.
* Provide “Download PNG” and “Download Video” buttons. Video export should create a short looping MP4 or WebM version of the animated card.
* Provide a “Share on X” button that prepares a short caption and profile link. If X cannot automatically attach the downloaded video without OAuth/API access, clearly instruct the user to attach the downloaded video manually.
* Every generated profile must have a shareable URL such as /agent/222 and social preview metadata.

Design:

* Premium minimal cyberpunk design inspired by the original IdentityMD visual language.
* Black and graphite background, neon colors derived from each NFT, crisp monospaced typography and restrained glow.
* Responsive on desktop and mobile.
* Clear loading, invalid token, missing NFT, offline API and unavailable-data states.
* Accessible controls and reduced-motion support.
* Cache public API responses briefly, but provide a Refresh button for current data.

Security and privacy:

* Read-only application.
* Never request a seed phrase, private key, token approval or transaction signature.
* Do not deploy a new token.
* Do not create financial contracts.
* Do not display VPS IP addresses, device keys, secrets or other private infrastructure data.

Deliver a complete working website connected to live public data, not a static mockup. Host the finished static frontend on IPFS and make sure all browser-side API requests work with CORS. If an official endpoint does not permit browser CORS, use an available browser-safe official endpoint or an onchain read-only fallback and document the limitation.

Deliver a complete working website connected to live public data, not a static mockup. Host the finished static frontend on IPFS and make sure all browser-side API requests work with CORS. If an official endpoint does not permit browser CORS, use an available browser-safe official endpoint or an onchain read-only fallback and document the limitation.

Improve the existing SIMCARD website. Do not rebuild it from scratch and do not remove the current animated card, token search, PNG/video download, profile links, QR code, or X sharing features.

1. Redesign the “Open profile” view

The current profile is too dark, text-heavy, and difficult to scan. Turn it into a clean dashboard made of clearly separated cards.

Use a slightly lighter charcoal background, brighter panels, clear borders, generous spacing, larger headings, and high-contrast text. Keep the current IdentityMD cyber style and each NFT’s dominant colors.

Use a two-column card grid on desktop and one column on mobile.

Display these sections as separate cards:

- Identity
- Live status
- Performance
- Rankings
- Rewards and launch allocations
- Work history
- Reviews
- Onchain verification links

Important numbers such as accepted work, acceptance rate, rank, rewards, and last activity should be visually prominent.

Do not display large paragraphs for unavailable data. Use a small muted “Unavailable” badge with a short explanation or tooltip instead.

Keep the animated SIMCARD visible at the top of the profile.

2. Fix the “Held for” calculation

The existing “Held for” value is incorrect. Calculate it from the Ethereum ERC-721 Transfer event in which the current owner most recently received this specific IdentityMD NFT.

Contract:
0x0000ec93127baa929e58e97dd0095a2bfb38ec1d

Do not use the agent pairing date, latest activity, API snapshot date, or unrelated contract activity.

Show both the readable duration and exact acquisition date, for example:

Held for: 34 days
Acquired: Aug 26, 2026

If the correct acquisition transaction cannot be verified, show “Unavailable” instead of an estimated or incorrect duration.

3. Improve live IdentityMD data handling

Retrieve the freshest available public data for the entered token ID from the official IdentityMD endpoints, including:

- /seats/:tokenId
- /seats/:tokenId/standing
- /seats/records
- /wallets/:ownerAddress/earnings
- the public Explorer agent page
- Ethereum onchain ownership, metadata, and Transfer logs

Show:

- online/offline state
- runtime
- queue
- last activity
- attempts
- accepted
- rejected
- failed
- pending
- acceptance rate
- accepted-work rank
- attempts rank
- acceptance-rate rank
- percentile
- payouts
- launch allocations
- recent work
- reviews

This remains a static IPFS frontend. If the official IdentityMD API blocks browser requests because of CORS, do not use an untrusted public CORS proxy and do not fabricate live values. Use verified onchain data plus the latest bundled snapshot, label snapshot values clearly with their timestamp, and keep a Refresh button for retrying the official API.

Structure the data-access code so a trusted first-party API proxy can be added later through one configurable base URL.

4. Improve usability

- Preserve token-ID search and direct hash routes such as #/agent/222.
- Make the profile readable without opening technical JSON.
- Place technical API and explorer links inside a compact collapsible “Verification” card.
- Add loading, invalid-token, unavailable-data, and network-error states.
- Maintain full mobile responsiveness and keyboard accessibility.
- Do not require a wallet connection.
- Do not expose private keys, API keys, or secrets.
- Ensure PNG and video exports still work after the redesign.
- Ensure the QR code and share link open the correct token profile.
- Keep the site name “SIMCARD” and the tagline “One card. Every agent. Verified onchain.”

Update the existing SIMCARD website. Preserve the current visual design, animated NFT card, routes, download buttons, QR code, X sharing, and responsive layout. This is a focused data-layer repair, not a redesign.

Replace the current failing browser API requests with the following public live IdentityMD sources:

1. Fetch `https://api.imd.fun/swarm` as the primary live source. This endpoint supports browser CORS and is cached for approximately 10 seconds. Find the requested seat by its NFT token ID and use it for live status, presence, agent ID, attempts, accepted, rejected, failed, pending, last activity, runtime and other available performance data.

2. Fetch `https://explorer.imd.fun/api/agents/{tokenId}` as a second live source. Use its available fields such as online status, owner, ownerName, held, attempts, accepted, jobs and lastAcceptedAt.

3. Use `https://api.imd.fun/seats/records` only as a fallback for statistics and rankings. Do not allow failure of this request to replace valid `/swarm` or Explorer data with “Unavailable.”

4. Calculate rankings client-side from the complete seat records when available:
   - rank by accepted work
   - rank by attempts
   - rank by acceptance rate, with the existing minimum-attempt rule
   - percentile

5. Keep Ethereum onchain reads as the authoritative source for NFT ownership, artwork and acquisition history. Calculate “Held for” from the latest ERC-721 Transfer event in which the current owner received this specific token. Do not calculate it from the site build date, snapshot date or agent pairing date.

6. Never show every field as unavailable because one endpoint failed. Merge successful results field by field. Use this priority:
   - live `/swarm` data
   - Explorer agent endpoint
   - onchain data
   - last valid snapshot
   - only then show “Unavailable” for that individual field

7. Add automatic refresh every 10 seconds for live status and statistics. Show a small “Live · updated X seconds ago” indicator. Preserve the last valid values during a temporary refresh failure.

8. Keep the Open Profile interface clean and organized in the existing card/grid layout. Do not return to a long text-heavy profile.

9. Display a small and clear data-source label for each section: “Live IMD,” “Explorer,” “Onchain,” or “Snapshot.” Do not expose technical error messages to normal users.

10. Test at least token IDs `222` and `1`. Confirm that one unavailable endpoint does not prevent the other public and onchain values from appearing.

Important: this is an IPFS-hosted static React frontend. Do not add a private backend, secret API key, wallet connection or paid API dependency. Keep the site fully read-only.

items.title:
Build and publish a website called:

IMDerivatives

PURPOSE

IMDerivatives is an independent directory of projects, tokens, NFTs,
strategies, apps and experiments built around or supporting the
Identity MD / IMD ecosystem.

The core idea:

BUILT AROUND IMD ≠ BUILT BY IMD.

This is NOT an official Identity MD website.

Do not imply that any project is official, endorsed, partnered with,
or approved by Identity MD unless a primary authoritative IMD source
explicitly proves that relationship.

Do not call a project fraudulent or a scam without strong verifiable
evidence.

Automated security warnings are risk signals, not proof of fraud.

DISCLAIMER

Display prominently:

"IMDerivatives is an independent community resource and is not
affiliated with Identity MD. Listed projects may be built by third
parties. Inclusion does not imply endorsement by Identity MD.
Always verify contracts and links independently."

Also display:

"Nothing on this site is financial advice."

INITIAL PROJECTS

Research and include these four projects.

1. SWARM PEPE

https://opensea.io/collection/swarm-pepe

Known contract to verify:
0x999ce0ce8c5f7661e0c74a568ffe27ceb9177bdb

Determine:
- what it does
- blockchain
- verified contract
- creator/provenance where possible
- relationship to IMD
- evidence of official IMD affiliation, if any
- risk signals
- evidence sources

Do not infer official affiliation merely because the project references
Identity MD holders or the IMD swarm.

2. IMD STRATEGY / TOKENWORKS

https://www.tokenstrategy.com/strategies/0x80271ce20184e38f4afe90d4ca134304d197aca2

Contract:
0x80271ce20184e38f4afe90d4ca134304d197aca2

Research TokenStrategy / TokenWorks documentation.

Explain what the strategy actually does and how it relates to
Identity MD NFTs.

Clearly distinguish TokenWorks from Identity MD.

Do not call it an official IMD product unless primary IMD evidence
explicitly establishes this.

3. PROJECT HIVE

https://projecthive.fun/dashboard.html

Research carefully.

Verify where possible:
- site behavior
- contracts
- chain
- creator/provenance
- relationship to IMD
- security warnings
- official IMD references

Automated warnings must be described as automated warnings, not proof
of fraud.

If important evidence cannot be verified, classify the project
UNVERIFIED and explain why.

Never invent contracts, affiliations, or security findings.

4. IMD STRATEGY / NOSH

https://www.usenosh.app/coins/0xE749C8Bf545DA0db1aA6664c63c072c96f25acA1

Token:
0xE749C8Bf545DA0db1aA6664c63c072c96f25acA1

Research Nosh documentation.

Explain:
- what the token/strategy does
- how it interacts with Identity MD / its NFTs
- chain
- relevant contracts
- creator/provenance where verifiable
- audit status
- risks and trust assumptions
- evidence of official IMD endorsement, if any

CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM

Give every project one primary status:

OFFICIAL IMD
Only when a primary Identity MD source explicitly establishes that
the project is official.

INDEPENDENT — VERIFIED
Project and relevant contracts are independently verifiable, but it
is not established as an official Identity MD product.

INDEPENDENT — SUPPORTS IMD
A third-party project whose mechanism supports, purchases, burns,
uses, funds, or otherwise interacts with IMD / Identity MD.

UNVERIFIED
Insufficient evidence exists to verify important claims.

FLAGGED
Specific credible security concerns have been identified.

Risk signals can additionally include:

UNAUDITED
NEW CONTRACT
NEW DOMAIN
UPGRADEABLE
ADMIN CONTROL
EXTERNAL KEEPER
AUTOMATED SECURITY WARNING
UNVERIFIED CONTRACT
WALLET CONNECTION
UNKNOWN TEAM

A risk signal must NEVER automatically mean "fraud".

ABSENCE FROM OFFICIAL IMD SOURCES ≠ FRAUD.

It means official affiliation has not been established.

EVIDENCE

Every important factual claim should have a source.

Prefer:

1. on-chain contracts and transactions
2. official Identity MD sources
3. project documentation
4. blockchain explorers
5. reputable independent sources
6. automated scanners/social posts as supporting context only

Clearly distinguish:

VERIFIED FACT
PROJECT CLAIM
THIRD-PARTY CLAIM
AUTOMATED WARNING
UNKNOWN

If sources disagree, show the disagreement.

Never fabricate missing evidence.

DESIGN

Create a polished dark cyber / terminal / subtle pixel-art aesthetic.

It should feel related to the autonomous-agent / on-chain world of
IMD without pretending to be an official IMD interface.

Responsive desktop + mobile.

Homepage hero:

IMDerivatives

"Map the ecosystem. Verify the relationship."

Secondary line:

"Built around IMD ≠ built by IMD."

Show ecosystem counters such as:

Projects
Official
Independent
Unverified
Flagged

Only show counters calculated from actual project data.

FILTERS

All
NFT
Token
Strategy
App
Official
Independent
Unverified
Flagged

PROJECT CARDS

Each card should show:

name
category
short description
affiliation status
risk badges
chain
contract/address when applicable
last reviewed date
external project link
detail/evidence button

PROJECT DETAIL

Each project page or expandable detail view should contain:

Overview

What does it do?

Why is this related to IMD?

Official or independent?

Contracts

How it works

Security / trust assumptions

Risk signals

Official endorsement evidence

Evidence & sources

Last reviewed

For addresses include copy buttons and blockchain explorer links.

External links should clearly indicate that the user is leaving
IMDerivatives.

For UNVERIFIED or FLAGGED projects, display a warning before the
external link.

SAFETY

The website is informational and read-only.

NO wallet connection.
NO trading.
NO swaps.
NO token approvals.
NO minting.
NO investment recommendations.
NO price predictions.

Do not create fake live metrics.

DATA

Keep all listings in a structured file such as:

projects.json

or

projects.ts

Each project should support:

id
name
category
description
relationshipToIMD
affiliationStatus
affiliationEvidence
chain
contracts
links
riskFlags
securityNotes
sources
lastReviewed

Make it easy to add future IMD ecosystem projects.

RESEARCH

Create RESEARCH.md documenting what was actually verified for every
listing and the sources used.

Do not silently convert assumptions into facts.

DELIVERABLE

Build and publish the complete static website.

Site name:

IMDerivatives

Return:

- public website URL
- repository/commit
- project data file
- RESEARCH.md
- build status
- publication evidence

The website succeeds if a visitor can quickly answer:

1. "What does this project have to do with IMD?"

2. "Is this actually an official Identity MD project, or an
independent project built around it?"

The site should be a neutral ecosystem map, not a promotional page.

Continue and update the existing IMDerivatives website from parent job:

a10bd012-c45d-4e03-8fcc-1f198aacc21c

Do NOT rebuild an unrelated site. Preserve the existing IMDerivatives design, research, project classifications, disclaimers, links and evidence model unless correcting a demonstrated error.

OBJECTIVE

Upgrade IMDerivatives into a more useful read-only ecosystem dashboard by adding verifiable market data for the listed projects.

IMDerivatives remains an independent community resource.

Built around IMD ≠ built by IMD.

Do not imply Identity MD endorsement or official affiliation unless supported by primary Identity MD evidence.

MARKET DATA

For every listed project, research whether reliable current market data exists.

Where applicable display:

- token price
- market capitalization
- 24h trading volume
- 24h price change
- circulating supply if reliably available
- chain
- contract address
- market-data source
- last updated timestamp

Prefer contract-address-based identification rather than matching only by token/project name.

Use reliable APIs or public market/on-chain sources.

Never invent market data.

If a metric cannot be reliably obtained, display:

N/A

Do not estimate a market cap from weak or incompatible data merely to fill the interface.

NFT projects and non-token applications may not have a directly comparable token market capitalization. Clearly distinguish these rather than manufacturing an equivalent value.

MARKET CAP VISUALIZATION

Add an ecosystem market-cap section.

Create a responsive donut/pie chart showing the relative market capitalization of eligible IMDerivatives projects.

Each slice represents one project.

Slice size must be calculated from:

project market cap / total market cap of all eligible projects

Example:

Project A = $5M
Project B = $3M
Project C = $2M

The chart should visually represent approximately:

50%
30%
20%

Do not hardcode percentages.

Calculate them from the current underlying data.

Show:

- project name
- project color
- market cap
- percentage of represented total

On hover/tap show the exact value and percentage.

In the center of the donut show:

Tracked Ecosystem Market Cap

and the sum of all eligible projects.

IMPORTANT:

The chart represents only projects with reliable, comparable market-cap data.

Clearly state:

"Chart includes only listed projects for which comparable market-cap data could be verified. It does not represent the total value of the Identity MD ecosystem."

Do not include N/A projects in the denominator.

VOLUME

Add a second ecosystem metric:

24h Tracked Volume

Calculate this only from projects with reliable 24h volume data.

On each eligible project card display its individual 24h volume.

Never treat NFT marketplace volume, token DEX volume and unrelated protocol TVL as if they were the same metric without clearly labeling the difference.

PROJECT CARDS

Enhance existing cards with a compact market-data section where applicable:

PRICE
MARKET CAP
24H VOLUME
24H CHANGE

Retain:

classification

risk flags
chain
contract

with the actual timestamp.

DATA PROVENANCE

SAFETY

Build BUILT BY THE SWARM: a static site showing what the IdentityMD network shipped, with media, a written daily issue and a protocol changelog, from public sources only. This job produces issue 1 (2026-09-29) and the site. Later issues come from daily jobs whose repository names start with "swarm-daily" and contain the same files; the site loads its bundled issue first, then discovers more from GitHub. This repository's name must start with "swarm-daily-site".

SOURCES (public, read-only; cite endpoint and UTC time per number): https://api.imd.fun/health, /launches (newest 500; /launches/:id for launches mentioned), /launch/policies, /jobs (newest 500), /oracle/requests, /schedules, /seats/records, /services, /sites, /skills, /version; https://explorer.imd.fun/api/activity; https://imd.fun/docs/; releases of https://github.com/identity-md/worker. Nothing else; no speculation; unavailable values are "not exposed".

DATA. Write data/2026-09-29/data.json with exactly these top-level keys (every numeric value an object {value, source, readAt}; missing values null): issue {date, number}; network {connectedDaemons, activeEnrollments, workingNow, acceptedLastDay, pendingFeedback, deployBreaker, payments{quoted, paid, expired, failed}}; launches {highestNumber, byStatus, last24h:[{id, number, name, kind, status, policyVersion, repo, pair}], parkedReasons:[{reason, count}]}; policies:[{version, kind, note, createdAt}]; jobs {last24hByKind, createdBySchedule}; oracle {last24hByStatus, exampleQuestions:[3 verbatim], models:[]}; schedules {active, items:[{label, action, cadence, runsRemaining}]}; seats {active24h, active7d, everWorked, top5:[{tokenId, accepted}]}; changelog {docsToc:[], docsRoutes:[], paidActions:[], skills:[], versionFeatures:[], services:[], workerRelease}; briefs {accepted:[{objective300, skill, minutesToAccept}], parked:[{objective300, skill, reason}]}; gallery:[{name, kind: token|contracts|hook|report|website|image|audio|video|oracle|heartbeat|community (the hire page's categories), asked (one sentence from the job objective), built (two sentences from the README and job record), media {type: screenshot|image|video|audio|none, src, poster}, links{site, repo, launch, job, cid}}]; sources:[{url, readAt}]. Commit the schema as data/schema.md. Previous issues are public GitHub repositories in identity-md-launches whose names start with "swarm-daily"; for issue 1 there are none, so deltas are null.

ISSUE. data/2026-09-29/issue.md, 700-1200 words, plain, no praise, lowercase headings, numbers first, in order: the network today (five headline numbers: seats online, seats with accepted work in 24h, launches opened in 24h, oracle requests attested in 24h, active schedules); launches (what went live and parked, reasons grouped, policies changed in the last 7 days quoted verbatim); what got built (each gallery item with its media where it has one, then one sentence on what was asked and two on what was built, from the job objective and the README); oracle and schedules (question categories with three verbatim examples, attested vs disagreed vs failed, active schedules); work and seats (jobs by kind, seat concentration top 5 and top 20 share, distinct seats ever); changelog (issue 1 has no previous issue, so build it from sources that carry their own dates, as dated entries: launch policies by createdAt, worker releases by publish date, sites by publish time, the current /version build; and record undated sources, docs TOC and routes, paid actions, skills, services, as a baseline labelled "as of 2026-09-29, diffs start next issue"); briefs that worked (three objectives accepted first try and one parked, 300 chars each with skill and time to acceptance, one sentence on the difference; no wallet addresses); watch list (max five checkable facts); sources.

MEDIA. Items for the day: every site published (from /sites), every launch that went live, every accepted image, audio, video and report job, the ten most recent oracle requests attested (question plus answer; the count of the rest goes in data.json), active heartbeats, and up to ten other accepted jobs, most recent first. Media per kind: website gets a 1280x800 screenshot with the assigned browser (dark theme if offered) saved to data/2026-09-29/media/<slug>.png; image jobs use the delivered image file copied into media/; video jobs copy the delivered file (or link it if over 20 MB) with a poster frame extracted into media/; audio jobs copy the file; everything else has media type none. If no browser is available, screenshots are null and cards link instead. Never capture anything requiring login.

SITE. Vite, React, TypeScript; relative paths and hash routing for IPFS and eth.limo. Quiet, document-like, monospace matching explorer.imd.fun, light and dark (prefers-color-scheme plus toggle). Runtime config.json next to index.html: githubOrg (default identity-md-launches), repoPrefix (default swarm-daily), communityLinks:[{name, url, oneLiner}]. Pages:
1. built (home): date header with the five headline numbers and a link to the issue; filters all and one per category; sort newest; a card grid typed by the hire page's categories. Every card carries its category glyph top-left over the media: a simple line icon per category in the style of the hire page's icons (inline SVG, drawn, not hotlinked), with the category name as a tooltip on hover and focus and as an accessible label; no text badge. Website cards show the screenshot; image cards show the image; video cards embed the video with its poster and native controls; audio cards show a tile with a native player; token, contracts, hook, report, oracle, heartbeat and community cards show a typed tile with one accent colour per category consistent in both themes and the name large; oracle tiles show the question and the attested answer, heartbeat tiles the label and cadence. Below the media: name, the "asked" sentence muted, the "built" sentences, and links: open, repo, launch, job or oracle page. Community cards come from config communityLinks.
2. issue: the rendered issue.md for the selected date with a date switcher.
3. changelog: dated entries newest first from every issue's changelog block, plus diffs between consecutive issues once more than one exists; the baseline is shown collapsed.
4. numbers: headline metrics per issue as a table; line charts once three or more issues exist.
Data loading: read ./data/index.json (bundled issue dates) and render at once; then query the GitHub search API for repositories in githubOrg named with repoPrefix, fetch each data.json and issue.md from raw.githubusercontent.com, merge by date; cache in memory; degrade gracefully on rate limits (bundled data plus "live index unavailable"). Tolerate missing fields. Safe markdown rendering; lazy media. Footer: "this site only reads public data. community built, not an official imd site."

DELIVERY. Production build and typecheck. Never fabricate gallery items; a category with no real item today shows its empty filter state. Browser-test desktop and mobile in both themes: home grid with the bundled issue, every filter, glyph tooltips on hover and keyboard focus, card links, issue page, changelog with dated entries and collapsed baseline, numbers table, GitHub discovery both working and with the network unavailable, hash routes reloaded directly, keyboard focus, console errors, failed resource loads. Exercise every card renderer (screenshot, image, video with poster, audio player, each tile type) with local test fixtures that are not shipped in dist. Fix defects. Commit source, lockfile, data/ (schema, issue 1 folder) and the completed dist/ including config.json and data/. Provide artifacts/validation.md and desktop-dark, desktop-light and mobile screenshots. Public GitHub source and a hosted IPFS preview are requested; choose a short lowercase label (3-32 chars, letters, digits, hyphens, no dates) that names the site, and record it in the README. No token, no contracts.

Release Badges (ERC-20 symbol BDGE) on Sepolia as an evm_project: the fixed-supply launch token plus one application contract. Token: Badges (BDGE), total supply 1,000,000,000 BDGE with 18 decimals, minted once to the deployer. Application contract: SoulboundBadges. Currency: creating a badge type burns 100 BDGE as an anti-spam fee. SoulboundBadges takes the BDGE address as its only constructor argument (constructorArgs ["$token"]), exposes it as token() and holds no BDGE at deploy or ever: the fee moves straight from the creator to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD with SafeERC20.safeTransferFrom after a BDGE ERC-20 approve (users get BDGE by swapping Sepolia ETH in the launch pool). No payable function, no owner, admin, pause or upgrade path. A Sepolia test toy: badges are not credentials, and the README and the page say so. SoulboundBadges is an OpenZeppelin ERC-721 with ERC721Enumerable, named "Soulbound Badges" with symbol "SBADGE" (source constants, not constructor arguments); badge type ids and token ids both start at 1 and increase by one. Tokens are soulbound per ERC-5192 (interface id 0xb45a3c0e): locked(tokenId) always returns true, Locked is emitted at mint, and badge transfers plus the badge contract's own ERC-721 approve and setApprovalForAll revert (burn is the only way a badge leaves its holder). createBadgeType(bytes32 name): the name must be 1-32 characters from [A-Za-z0-9 _-] right-padded with zero bytes (anything else reverts, which keeps the on-chain JSON and SVG safe to render); burns the 100 BDGE fee; the caller becomes the type's issuer. Names need not be unique, so the site always shows the type id and issuer next to a name. setIssuer(typeId, newIssuer): current issuer only, non-zero. award(typeId, to): issuer only; one live badge per (type, holder); to != address(0). burn(tokenId): the holder only; afterwards the issuer may award that type to them again. Actors: anyone creates a badge type; only a type's current issuer awards it or hands it over; only a holder burns its badge; any other call reverts. tokenURI reverts for a burned or unminted id and otherwise returns on-chain base64 JSON (name, type id, issuer, image) with a generated SVG showing the badge name and a colour derived from the type id. Views: badgeType(typeId) returning (name, issuer), typeCount(), badgeOf(typeId, holder) returning the holder's live badge token id or 0, typeOf(tokenId), tokenOfOwnerByIndex, supportsInterface (721, 721Enumerable, 5192). Events: TypeCreated(typeId, name, issuer), IssuerChanged, Transfer and Locked from the standards. Tests (Foundry) must cover: badge transferFrom, both safeTransferFrom variants, ERC-721 approve and setApprovalForAll all reverting, the name charset check, the fee burn (the contract never holds BDGE), duplicate awards refused, holder-only burn and re-award, issuer handover, tokenURI decoding to valid JSON with an SVG, and supportsInterface for ERC-5192. The independent adversarial review must attack: any path that moves a badge (safeTransferFrom variants, approvals), JSON/SVG injection through the name, awarding a type you do not issue, and the fee being skippable. Deploy through the project factory, then publish a one-page website to create a badge type (approve 100 BDGE), award badges, and show a profile page of any address's badges. The page shows the connected wallet's BDGE balance and allowance and says BDGE comes from swapping Sepolia ETH in the launch pool. Lists come from contract views and events only (no backend, no indexer). Keep it to one small page; the static export has index.html in dist/.

Build THE DOCKET, a calm, fast, static site where people shape job ideas for the IMD swarm and discuss what it has built. The only backend is the Docket v0.1 contract from https://github.com/identity-md-launches/launch-197-build-docket-v0-1-smallest (README, ABI and events are the source of truth). The requester deploys it on Ethereum mainnet and Base using this site's own deploy page after delivery, so all deployment details come from a runtime configuration file. Visitors connect any wallet, read, post ideas or comments, upvote either, and attach an idea to anything the swarm has produced. Apply the better-interface reference.

VISUAL DIRECTION
Quiet, legible, document-like; one accent. Match the monospace typeface and weights of explorer.imd.fun (inspect its stylesheet; self-host the same family or the nearest open-licensed equivalent, no font CDN). Light and dark themes, both fully designed, default from prefers-color-scheme, header toggle persisted in localStorage, no flash of wrong theme. Desktop shows the idea list beside the open idea; mobile stacks them with a back control. UI vocabulary: "job ideas" for the list, "idea" in the singular, "new idea" for the create action; never "thread" or "post" in visible copy.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOUR
1. Reads work without a wallet. Reconstruct ideas, comments and upvotes purely from IdeaCreated, CommentPosted and Upvoted events (subjects parsed per item 3) on both deployments via configurable RPC URLs, scanning from each deployment block, chunked for public RPC limits, with a small in-browser cache; merge into one list by time; identify ideas by (chainId, ideaId). If one chain's RPC fails, mark its ideas unavailable with a retry control while the other renders; never a blank page.
2. Connect any wallet (injected and WalletConnect via viem/wagmi). No forced network switch on connect; the user posts on whichever supported chain the wallet is on; on any other chain, prompt to switch to Base (default) or mainnet.
3. New idea: title and body with live byte counters and client-side length validation (120 and 4000 bytes), plus an optional subject. The contract has no subject field, so the subject is a body convention: when set, the composer writes it as the body's first line in the exact form "subject: <ref>" (refs job:<uuid>, launch:<n>, agent:<tokenId>, oracle:<uuid>; small picker plus free text); the reader strips that line and treats it as the subject; the 4000-byte limit includes it. Subjects render as a chip linking to the matching explorer.imd.fun page (jobs/<uuid>, launches/<n>, agents/<tokenId>, oracle/<uuid>); #/s/<ref> lists ideas on that subject under a small live card fetched read-only from the public endpoints when cross-origin reads are permitted (api.imd.fun/jobs/<uuid>: state, template, objective excerpt, repo; explorer.imd.fun/api/agents/<tokenId>: online, accepted, attempts), falling back to the plain link if the fetch fails; home filters: all / free / on jobs / on launches / on agents. Copy says "on job …", never "thread". Sends createIdea on the wallet's current chain. Chain is a cost of posting, never a property of the idea: on mainnet the composer says posting costs real gas and offers a one-click switch to Base (a fraction of a cent); on Base, say nothing. Pending/confirmed/failed inline; the idea appears without reload.
4. Comment: ideas are chain-local, so comments go to the idea's chain; if the wallet is elsewhere, the composer offers a one-click switch, explained as cost, not location. Body 1–2000 bytes, same validation; appears on confirmation without reload; comments render newest last. No chain markers in the list or idea header; the only chain cue outside the composer is a muted "on mainnet" in the metadata line of ideas stored on mainnet, so readers understand reply costs. The storage chain must never read as the chain a job targets.
5. Author display: truncated address or ENS name via the mainnet RPC. Beside each author, compact badges read from Ethereum mainnet, cached per session: identitymd NFT balance (0x0000ec93127baa929e58e97dd0095a2bfb38ec1d) shown as seats, IMD balance (0xd34a99bc0f67ae1bbd63c660e6d0b0dd03e263b7), sIMD balance (0x9Efa934D9fAd4AE28c998a40195646b965a97247) shown as staked. Upvotes: a control on every idea (list and header) and every comment, disabled once the wallet has voted; sends upvote(ideaId, commentId), commentId 0 for the idea. Two counts per target: all upvotes, and upvotes from wallets meeting the gate threshold (from cached badge reads). The idea list sorts by holder-upvotes by default with a toggle for newest; comments sort chronologically by default with a toggle for holder-upvotes.
6. Soft write gate, frontend only: composers and upvote controls are enabled only when the connected wallet holds at least 1 identitymd seat or more than 100 IMD on mainnet (IMD plus sIMD). Otherwise show controls disabled with a one-line explanation and a link to imd.fun. Thresholds and token addresses come from config.json. Reading is never gated. Courtesy filter, not security; the contract accepts posts from any address.
7. Plain-text rendering only, links shown as text, never embedded; long bodies collapse; keyboard navigable; visible focus; no dead controls. Footer, exact copy: "this site only reads messages posted onchain by their authors. community built, not an official imd site."
8. Deploy page at #/deploy: embeds the exact Docket creation bytecode from the referenced repo (solc 0.8.26, optimizer 200, cancun, bytecode_hash none); the connected wallet deploys a fresh Docket on its current chain; show tx, address, deployment block, the standard-JSON compiler input and exact verification settings. Explain that this board is ignored until config.json points at it.
config.json next to index.html, fetched at startup, holds: per-chain address, chain id, deployment block and RPC URL, the mainnet RPC for badges and ENS, and gate thresholds and token addresses. Ship both chain entries with empty addresses. A chain with no address renders an "unconfigured" state linking to #/deploy; if neither is configured the home page shows that state instead of an empty list. Editing config.json and re-publishing the same static files must be the only step to point at real deployments; the README documents this without build tooling.

SCOPE
No accounts, backend, database, indexer, analytics, cookies, gas sponsorship, signatures beyond wallet transactions, moderation, editing/deleting, idea status, structured drafts or contract changes; the deploy page deploys the unmodified Docket bytecode only. No extra features.

REVIEW AND DELIVERY
Build with Vite, React and TypeScript; relative asset paths and hash routing so it works from an IPFS gateway and via eth.limo. Run the production build and typecheck. Browser-test desktop and mobile in both themes against two local Anvil chains with a Docket deployed from the referenced repo on each, plus the unconfigured state: read without wallet with both chains merged, one RPC failing, connect without forced switch, unsupported-network prompt, cost nudge and switch, gate disabled and enabled states, create a free idea and one with a job: subject, open its subject page and filter, comment, upvote an idea and a comment and confirm the second attempt is blocked, deploy from #/deploy to an Anvil chain and confirm address and block, oversized input rejection, retry state, keyboard focus, console errors, failed resource loads. Fix observed defects. Commit source, lockfile, README (every config.json field, the re-publish procedure, how to use #/deploy) and the completed dist/ including the template config.json. Provide artifacts/validation.md (commands, viewports, evidence, findings/fixes, limitations), artifacts/desktop-dark.png, artifacts/desktop-light.png, artifacts/mobile.png, and artifacts/website.zip with index.html at its root. Public GitHub source and a hosted IPFS preview under the label "docket" are requested.

Build and launch a token-gated membership project on Sepolia, end to end: contracts, token and pool, a public GitHub repository, and a website hosted on IPFS.

Contracts (Foundry, with tests and an independent adversarial review):
- The project token: a fixed-supply ERC-20 whose name and symbol you choose to fit a membership club.
- A membership badge contract: an ERC-721 where any address holding at least a threshold balance of the token can mint exactly one badge for itself. The threshold is set at deployment. A badge is soulbound (non-transferable). Anyone can check whether an address is currently eligible and whether it holds a badge. If a holder later falls below the threshold the badge stays, but a view reports it as lapsed.
- Emit events for mints so the site can list members.

Launch: deploy the token and the badge contract as an evm_project on Sepolia and seed the token pool, so the token can be bought to qualify.

Website (static, hosted on IPFS, reading the deployed addresses from the launch handoff): connect a wallet on Sepolia, show the token balance against the threshold, a link to buy the token on the pool, a mint button when eligible, the badge once minted, and a public member list built from mint events with lapsed members marked.

Build and independently review Duel Arena, a playable non-hook rock-paper-scissors escrow game, for automatic Sepolia deployment through the evm_project launch pipeline. Deliver a complete standalone Foundry project with source, meaningful tests, README, and artifacts/report.md. This job requests GitHub publication, an admitted on-chain deployment, and named registry artifacts. Contributors must never read wallet keys or broadcast transactions; the configured deployer handles the accepted release.

Deploy exactly two authored contracts: DuelToken and DuelArena. Follow the pinned evm-project-launch reference and Sepolia policy v3. DuelToken is a conventional fixed-supply ERC-20 named "Duel Arena", symbol "DUEL", 18 decimals, with NO constructor arguments and exactly 1,000,000,000 tokens (10^27 base units) minted to msg.sender in its constructor. No mint, tax, pause, blacklist, upgrade, or admin functions. DuelArena is non-upgradeable, uses only this token, has no administrator, platform fees, oracle, randomness service, or privileged withdrawal. Constructor parameters are (address token_, uint64 joinWindow_, uint64 revealWindow_); launch arguments must be ["$token","3600","3600"]. Validate the constructor inputs and complete all setup there. Use Solidity 0.8.26, bytecode_hash = "none", offline-buildable dependencies, and no ffi or filesystem permissions. No frontend, badges, NFT collection, or additional game modes in this iteration.

Game:
- A creator chooses a positive token stake and either a specific different opponent or address(0) for an open duel. Creator escrows one stake and submits a nonzero commitment when creating. Reject zero stakes, self-opponents, and amounts that could overflow pot accounting.
- Use bytes32 duelId = keccak256(abi.encode(creator, nonce)). Creation supplies the expected per-creator nonce, checks it, then consumes it atomically. Provide getters/helpers so clients can derive the ID and commitment without a separate reservation transaction. IDs cannot be reused after terminal states.
- Commitment must be keccak256(abi.encode(block.chainid, address(this), duelId, player, uint8(move), bytes32(salt))), with move 0=rock, 1=paper, 2=scissors. Domain-bind every component and document a fresh unpredictable 32-byte salt per move. Show how to compute commitments locally without publishing a move or salt before reveal.
- Join deadline is creation timestamp + joinWindow. A permitted opponent other than creator joins before that deadline, commits their move, and escrows exactly the same stake. No third player, second join, commitment replacement, or stake edits. Reveal deadline is successful join timestamp + revealWindow. Both commitments exist before any reveal is accepted.
- Joining and revealing require timestamp < the applicable deadline; expiry/timeout finalization requires timestamp >= deadline. Reject invalid moves, wrong salts/player/domain/duel, repeat reveals, early reveals, and late reveals without consuming a valid future action.
- Settle as soon as the second valid reveal arrives: winner receives a withdrawal credit of the entire pot; equal moves give each player their original stake as credit.
- After the reveal deadline, anyone may finalize. Exactly one valid reveal awards the whole pot to that revealer; no reveals returns each original stake. After an unmatched duel's join deadline, anyone may expire it and credit the creator's stake. There is no cancellation function. All terminal transitions happen exactly once.
- Use pull withdrawals with clear events and checks-effects-interactions/reentrancy protection. A failed transfer must preserve the user's credit, and reentry must not enable duplicate claims. Track total liability (active escrow + withdrawal credits): settlement preserves it, withdrawals reduce it, and token balance always covers it. Unexpected direct token transfers are surplus with no privileged recovery. Do not advertise arbitrary rebasing/fee-token compatibility.
- Persist readable duel state, deadlines, revealed moves only after valid reveal, outcome, credits, and per-player wins/losses/draws/forfeits. Ordinary winner/loser receive W/L; equal moves give each a draw; sole revealer receives W and opponent L plus a forfeit; neither reveals gives each a forfeit but no W/L/draw; unmatched expiry changes no competitive stats. State explicitly that this is an address-based record, not Sybil-resistant reputation.

Validation:
Meaningful Foundry tests must cover all nine move pairs; open and designated opponents; creator nonce races/reuse and multiple concurrent duels; domain/replay separation by chain, arena, duel and player; all deadline boundaries including exact equality; invalid/duplicate/out-of-order actions; both timeout outcomes and unmatched expiry; double settlement/withdrawal; isolated escrow between games; failed withdrawals and attempted reentrancy; conservation of token balances and liabilities. Include bounded fuzz/property coverage of accounting and state transitions. Verify the token's exact supply and lack of privileged minting. Run forge build, forge test and forge fmt --check offline. Document actual checks and remaining limitations in artifacts/report.md.

README must explain the architecture, state/outcome table, timeout lock-up tradeoff, token acquisition through contributor claims or an existing holder/pool (no faucet mint backdoor), approvals, and ready-to-use cast examples for two wallets to create, join, reveal, inspect, finalize and withdraw. Use placeholders for deployed addresses and wallet credentials; never embed real secrets. Do not execute the examples against a public chain. Document the arena/token constructor and commitment ABI exactly.

The separate manifest assignment writes launch.json using kind evm_project, DuelToken, and DuelArena with the arguments above; use the reference's hookless native-ETH Sepolia pool parameters. The final independent reviewer must inspect accepted source, tests and manifest together, reproduce concrete escrow/commitment/deadline/permission failures, and raise blocking findings for real defects before release. Passing the protected deployment floor alone does not establish game correctness.
